cards.text: The soldiers are leading Jesus away. On the road, they seize a man named Simon of Cyrene, who's on his way in from the country. One minute he's walking into town minding his business, and the next minute soldiers have him by the arm.

cards.question: The soldiers grab Simon of Cyrene off the road. What do they make him do?

answers.text: Lead the way to the city gate
Hold back the crowd on the road

cards.text: Simon's not the only one following. A great number of people follow Jesus, including women who keep mourning and wailing for Him.

cards.question: Jesus turns to the women weeping for Him and tells them not to weep for Him. Who does He tell them to weep for instead?

cards.text: He calls them "Daughters of Jerusalem." He warns that days are coming when people will call the women who never had children blessed, and they'll say to the mountains, "Fall on us!"
Then He leaves them with one more line: "For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?"

cards.question: Jesus isn't the only one led away to be executed. The two others led away with Him are two of His disciples.

cards.text: Then they arrive. Friend, this place has a name that sends a chill right down your apron strings.

cards.question: They come to the place called The ___.

cards.text: They crucify Him there, along with the criminals. One is on His right and the other on His left.

cards.question: Hanging on the cross, Jesus speaks to His Father. What does He ask?

answers.text: Forgive them because they don't know what they're doing
Judge them for everything they have done to Me
Take Me down from this cross before the night

cards.question: Right there below Jesus, they divide up His garments by casting ___.

cards.text: The people stand there watching. The rulers sneer at Him: "He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One."
The soldiers mock Him too. They come up and offer Him sour wine.

cards.question: The soldiers' taunt sounds a lot like the rulers' sneer. What do the soldiers say to Jesus?

answers.text: If You are the King of the Jews save Yourself
If You are a prophet tell us who hit You
If You are the Son of God call down fire

cards.question: The inscription posted above Jesus on the cross calls Him the King of the Jews.

cards.text: Jesus is on the cross, with a criminal hanging on each side. One of them heaps abuse on Him. "Are You not the Christ?" he says. "Save Yourself and us!"

cards.question: The other criminal hanging beside Jesus joins right in and mocks Him too.
The second criminal rebukes the first one. What does he say about the punishment the two of them are getting?

answers.text: It is just for what they did
It is far too harsh for them
It is a mistake by the soldiers

cards.question: Then the second criminal says about Jesus, "But this man has done nothing ___."

cards.text: Then he turns to Jesus: "Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!" Friend, the man is hanging on a cross, and he's asking about a KINGDOM.

cards.question: The criminal asks Jesus to remember him. What does Jesus promise him?

answers.text: Today you will be with Me in Paradise
Someday you will see My kingdom come
Tonight you will be taken down and freed

cards.text: It's now about the sixth hour. Darkness comes over all the land until the ninth hour, and the sun is darkened.

cards.question: While the sun is darkened, something happens at the temple. What happens to the temple's veil?

answers.text: It is torn down the middle
It is rolled up and hidden

cards.question: Then Jesus calls out to His Father in a loud voice. What does He say?

answers.text: Into Your hands I commit My Spirit
Send Your angels to take Me down
Let this darkness end right now

cards.text: And when He had said this, He breathed His last. Friend, let that one sit for a second.

cards.question: A centurion, a Roman army officer, sees what happened. He gives glory to God.
The centurion says, "Surely this was a ___ man."

cards.text: A whole crowd gathered to watch this spectacle. Now they've seen what happened.

cards.question: The crowd that gathered for the spectacle heads home. How do they go?
Everyone who knew Jesus, including the women who followed Him from Galilee, stands right beside the cross.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Hold on, friend. This story is NOT over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Daughters of Jerusalem.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "But this man has done nothing ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "Surely this was a ___ man.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-story, but the opening card only says the soldiers are leading Jesus away. It never says where or why: that He has been handed over to be crucified. Without that context, card 2's answer (carry the cross) is luck rather than an informed guess.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The setup says the place has a name that sends a chill down your spine. That rules out the wrong answers on card 9 (Pavement, Garden) and leaves Skull as the only chilling option.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Several story cards are flat retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 6, 10 and 14, and stop 2 cards 7 and 13. Jokes may not suit the crucifixion, but these cards are stripped down to plain summary, with no storyteller line, reaction or fatherly aside.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The statement 'The other criminal hanging beside Jesus joins right in and mocks Him too' is false in Luke 23:40. However, Matthew 27:44 says the robbers crucified with Him both berated Him, so a baker who knows Matthew could argue it is true.
findings.question: Should true/false statements and wrong answers avoid details that a parallel Gospel account makes true, or is the passage itself the only standard?

findings.problem: The statement that everyone who knew Jesus, including the Galilean women, stands right beside the cross is false in Luke 23:49 (at a distance). However, John 19:25-26 places His mother, other women and the disciple He loved near the cross, so a baker could argue part of it is true.
findings.question: Should true/false statements avoid claims that a parallel Gospel account contradicts, or is the passage itself the only standard?

findings.problem: A right pick of 'False' only tells the baker the women were not beside the cross. No card ever tells them that all who knew Jesus, including the women from Galilee, stood at a distance watching (Luke 23:49). The final story card could carry this before the closing line.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The closing line reuses the doc's example wording word for word: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from Luke 23:49, yet it cites Luke 23:49. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a final story card that is only the 'story isn't over' line?
